files.purpose: The MCP tab of Settings: a lead explainer card, a 'Connected' section of rows, a 'Custom' section with an add/edit popover, and per-category two-column grids of catalog server cards where one click connects. Also defines the shared MCPIcon view, the hover/click 'i' info button, the server details popover, monospaced tool chips and the FlowLayout they wrap with.

feature_notes: Connection celebration: when model.mcp.states flips an id to connected, the id is inserted into `celebrating`, SettleChime.play() fires, and after a 900ms Task.sleep it is removed, so the card flashes success in the grid and then moves to the 'Connected' section. The whole block is guarded by `guard !reduceMotion else { return }`, so with Reduce Motion the card moves straight across with no flash and no chime.
Grid animation: .animation(.spring(duration: 0.35), value: celebrating) with .transition(.scale(scale: 0.9).combined(with: .opacity)) on each card.
Search matching is case-insensitive over entry.name, entry.vendor, entry.summary, entry.id and any sampleTools element; an empty or whitespace-only query matches everything.
The Custom section hides itself completely while searching when no custom server matches; when not searching it always shows, with the explainer row when the user has none.

Connect flow (identical in MCPServerCard.begin() and MCPCustomRow.begin()): `!entry.needsInput` connects immediately via model.mcp.connect(entry); otherwise MCPKeyPanel.shared.present takes the field values.
A card whose state becomes .needsSetup auto-presents MCPSetupPanel with no user action, because the user just came back from the browser expecting a result.

Custom editor save(): builds `draft`; records wasConnected; model.mcp.saveCustom(draft, replacing: server?.id ?? savedID) and on failure sets error = failure.message and returns; sets savedID = draft.id; writes values with saveCustomValues(keptValues, for: draft.id, replacingFieldsOf: server?.catalogEntry()) and on failure shows the literal 'The Keychain could not save a value. Keep this editor open and try again.'; if it was connected and model.mcp.entry(for: draft.id) resolves, calls refresh; then dismiss().
savedID exists so a retry after a failed first save replaces the record just created rather than adding a duplicate.

Argument parsing: argsText is split on newline, lines that are whitespace-only after trimming are dropped, but surviving lines are NOT trimmed, so a leading dash, embedded spaces or quotes reach the server exactly as typed.
Variable keys are trimmed with .whitespaces; rows whose key is empty are dropped silently in both `draft` and `keptValues` rather than failing validation.
Switching kind preserves the variable list: the same keys become env vars for stdio or headers for http.

Editing pre-loads stored values on appear via model.mcp.storedValue(server:field:secret:); name focus is taken only when adding (server == nil), never when editing, so it does not read as a prompt to rename.
VariableDraft's identity is a UUID, deliberately not the key, because the key changes on every keystroke and would throw the row out of the ForEach mid-edit.

Hover info button: opens 220ms after the pointer arrives and closes 320ms after it has left BOTH the button and the popover, so the gap between them can be crossed; clicking cancels the pending settle and toggles immediately.
The tools popover and the custom edit popover are attached to the ellipsis button rather than the row, deliberately, because hung from the row they opened from the row's middle.
Connected rows are sorted alphabetically by entry.name; grid section order follows MCPCatalog.byCategory.
MCPCustomRow shows the SettingsSwitch only in the .connected state, whereas MCPConnectedRow shows it always (it only exists for connected entries).

feature_notes: present() opens the guide page in the browser BEFORE the panel appears, so the steps sit beside the page.

isPresenting(entry) guards re-entry: if the same entry's panel is already visible, present() only calls orderFrontRegardless and returns, so a failing re-check never reopens the browser page or rebuilds the steps under the user.
The NSPanel instance is reused across entries (`self.panel ?? makePanel()`); only contentViewController and size are replaced, and the escape monitor is installed at most once.
Escape (keyCode 53) closes the panel and the key event is consumed (the monitor returns nil).
Traffic lights are hidden deliberately because there is no title bar to hold them; closing is via the xmark button or Escape.
Pressing the guide.pageLabel button re-opens guide.pageURL in the browser.
'Check again' sets checkedOnce = true and calls model.mcp.refresh(entry); the follow-up status line only renders when checkedOnce is true and the probe is not currently connecting.
On connection the body swaps to successView and .onChange(of: state.isConnected) schedules onDone() 1.2 seconds later, which closes the panel.
Under accessibilityReduceMotion the success checkmark is set to full scale immediately rather than springing; unlike MCPServerCard, this view still shows the success state.
onGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self) { $0.size.height } reports the content height to MCPSetupPanel.shared.fit, so the panel follows content growth (the status line, the success view).
The whole background is a WindowDragArea, so a press anywhere the controls do not claim (reason text, steps, status line) drags the panel clear of the browser page behind it.
stepRow declares an `accessory: AnyView? = nil` parameter that no call site in this file supplies: unused/reserved code, reachable only if a future call passes it.
unresolved_questions: MCPSetupGuide's declaration and where guides are produced are outside this file; `note` is optional and its typical text is unknown.
Chrome.windowCornerRadius's numeric value is defined elsewhere.
WindowBackdrop's material and WindowDragArea's hit-testing rules are defined elsewhere; only opacity 0.5 is fixed here.

feature_notes: Filtering is deliberately instant with NO transitions: the comment records that animating dozens of rows with blur on every keystroke (and again on clearing) made entries overlap and jump.
matches() tests shortName, name, detail, the raw model id and provider.displayName with localizedCaseInsensitiveContains; an empty query matches everything.

The pinned list uses a plain VStack, not the card's lazy stack, on purpose: a lazy stack rebuilds a row that changes slot and animates it in from the container origin (sending the grabbed row flying to the top) and also ignores zIndex, which the lifted row needs.

Drag reorder: DragGesture(minimumDistance: 1, coordinateSpace: .global) on the grip only; the translation is applied inside a Transaction with disablesAnimations = true so the grabbed row tracks the pointer exactly, while neighbour swaps animate with .spring(response: 0.28, dampingFraction: 0.82).

The visible order is recomputed on every move via visiblePins(query:) rather than captured in the gesture, so swaps happen against the currently visible neighbour and hidden (filtered-out) models keep their relative place through settings.moveModel(pin, to: neighbour, placeAfter:).
RowDrag.settle is passed fallbackHeight: 54 for rows whose height has not been measured yet.
A landed swap fires NSHapticFeedbackManager .alignment at .now.
Drag end animates drag back to a fresh RowDrag() with .spring(response: 0.32, dampingFraction: 0.8) and pops the closed-hand cursor; it returns early when drag.id is nil.

Cursor bookkeeping: the open-hand push is popped on the grip's onDisappear and on isDragged going false while the pointer is not over the grip, covering the case where the drag is released away from the grip with no leave event.
rowHeights is pruned in .onChange(of: pins) whenever the dictionary holds more entries than pins, so an unpinned model takes its measured height with it.
Adding to and removing from the picker animate with Chrome.panelSlide.
Each ProviderModelsSection runs `.task { await registry.loadCatalog(provider) }`, so catalogs load lazily as sections appear; the 'Load models' button forces a reload with force: true.
A provider section is listed only when the trimmed query is empty or at least one of its models matches the query.
The whole 'Your models' section is skipped when a search matches none of the pinned models (`trimmed.isEmpty || !visiblePins.isEmpty`).

The effort and fast-mode bindings read and write through settings.preference/setPreference on every get and set rather than holding local copies, so the popover always reflects stored state; onReset writes a default ModelPreference().

files.purpose: A small @MainActor @Observable object that tracks whether a settings pane is being scrolled right now, reports that to the global ScrollActivity under one fixed pane UUID so effects that should not run under a moving finger rest, and exposes a separate isFrozen flag that tells settings rows to stop hovering and animating while content slides under the pointer.
state_owned: settle: Task<Void, Never>? (@ObservationIgnored, the debounce task)
side_effects: Registers and unregisters with the global ScrollActivity.shared singleton under the fixed pane UUID
Spawns a @MainActor Task that sleeps 150 milliseconds as the settle debounce, cancelling the previous one on each note()
platform_assumptions: Swift Observation (@Observable, @ObservationIgnored) and @MainActor isolation
Structured concurrency with Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(150)) and Task.isCancelled
Assumes a caller that can distinguish an active drag or wheel movement from a coasting flick, which on macOS comes from NSEvent scroll phase and momentum phase
ui_elements: No views: it drives row hover suppression through isFrozen and effect pausing through isScrolling elsewhere
feature_notes: note() is documented as 'a frame of movement': the first call flips isScrolling true and calls ScrollActivity.shared.setScrolling(true, timeline: Self.pane, reporter: self); every call restarts a 150ms debounce, after which isScrolling and isCoasting go false, isFrozen is cleared if set, and ScrollActivity is told scrolling stopped.
isFrozen is raised in note() only when `!isCoasting && !isFrozen`, so once the flick is coasting, further momentum frames do not re-freeze the rows.
coast() sets isCoasting = true and clears isFrozen immediately, so a click that stops a flick always reaches its target; the comment names this 'the chat timeline's rule'.
end() cancels the settle task, sets it to nil, clears isFrozen and isCoasting, then `guard isScrolling else { return }` so it only reports scrolling stopped when it had reported it started.
The pane key is a single `private static let pane = UUID()` shared by every instance, so all settings panes report under one timeline id rather than one per instance.
The settle task guards `guard let self, !Task.isCancelled else { return }` before mutating state, and captures self weakly.
unresolved_questions: The callers of note(), coast() and end() are not in this file, so which NSEvent phases map to coast() versus note() cannot be confirmed here.
ScrollActivity.shared's semantics - what pauses when a timeline reports scrolling and what the `reporter:` argument is used for - are defined elsewhere.
Whether isFrozen is consumed by every settings row or only some is not determinable from this file.
